```{r}
#| label: setup

library(ggplot2)

```

## Introduction

A good way to view Kolam construction is to take a parent-child sort of operation: we plot the Voronoi diagram of the grid of points, and then following Gopalan[], we selectively remove some of the boundaries of the Voronoi. We can also add an artistic dimension, but "curving out" the trajectories so that they *encircle the pulli-s* rather than dart past them. 

### Step 1: Voronoi of a general grid

If we plot a grid of points on a square grid, then it should be clear that the Voronoi boundaries of the assemblage of points is simply the perpendicular-bisectors of the segments joining adjacent points. See @fig-arbitrary-grid-voronoi below:

::: {.panel-tabset .nav-pills style="background: whitesmoke; "}

#### With R
```{r}
#| label: fig-arbitrary-grid-voronoi
#| fig-cap: "Grid of Points with Voronoi Boundaries"
#| code-fold: true
#| warning: false
#| 


pts <- expand.grid(x = 1:5, y = 1:3)

ggplot(pts, aes(x, y)) +
  geom_voronoi_tile(aes(fill = interaction(x, y)),
                    bound = c(0.5, 5.5, 0.5, 3.5),
                    colour = "white", show.legend = FALSE) +
  geom_voronoi_segment(bound = c(0.5, 5.5, 0.5, 3.5), colour = "black") +
  geom_point(colour = "firebrick", size = 3) +
  coord_fixed() +
  labs(title = "Rectangular Grid with Voronoi Boundaries") + 
  theme_minimal()

```

#### With p5.js
```{=html}
<div id="p5-step1"></div>
<script>
(function () {
  const HOST = 'p5-step1';
  const NX = 5, NY = 3, S = 110, M = 40;               // grid size, px per unit, margin
  const sx = x => M + (x - 0.5) * S;                   // data -> canvas (y flipped to match R)
  const sy = y => M + (NY + 0.5 - y) * S;

  function allEdges() {                                // every interior Voronoi edge
    const e = [];
    for (let y = 1; y <= 3; y++) for (let x = 1; x <= 4; x++) e.push([x + .5, y - .5, x + .5, y + .5]);
    for (let y = 1; y <= 2; y++) for (let x = 1; x <= 5; x++) e.push([x - .5, y + .5, x + .5, y + .5]);
    return e;
  }

  new p5(function (p) {
    p.setup = function () {
      p.createCanvas(NX * S + 2 * M, NY * S + 2 * M);
      p.colorMode(p.HSB, 360, 100, 100);
      p.noLoop();
    };
    p.draw = function () {
      p.background(0, 0, 100);
      p.noStroke();
      for (let j = 1; j <= NY; j++) for (let i = 1; i <= NX; i++) {   // pastel cells
        p.fill((((j - 1) * NX + (i - 1)) * 24) % 360, 25, 100);
        p.rect(sx(i - 0.5), sy(j + 0.5), S, S);
      }
      p.stroke(0, 0, 0); p.strokeWeight(3); p.strokeCap(p.SQUARE);
      allEdges().forEach(([x1, y1, x2, y2]) => p.line(sx(x1), sy(y1), sx(x2), sy(y2)));
      p.noFill(); p.strokeWeight(5);
      p.rect(sx(0.5), sy(3.5), NX * S, NY * S);                       // bounding rectangle
      p.noStroke(); p.fill(0, 85, 70);
      for (let j = 1; j <= NY; j++) for (let i = 1; i <= NX; i++) p.circle(sx(i), sy(j), 9);
    };
  }, document.getElementById(HOST) || undefined);
})();
</script>
```

:::


### Step 2: Random Modification to Voronoi

If we were to randomly drop Voronoi boundary edges between some pairs of adjacent points, we would get something like this:

::: {.panel-tabset .nav-pills style="background: whitesmoke; "}

#### With R
```{r}
#| label: fig-arbitary-mirrors
#| code-fold: true
#| fig-cap: "Grid with 2-Way mirrors"
#| warning: false
#| 

set.seed(42)

pts <- expand.grid(x = 1:5, y = 1:3)

# Vertical edges: separate horizontally adjacent points (4 x 3 = 12 edges)
v_edges <- with(expand.grid(x = 1:4, y = 1:3),
  data.frame(x = x + 0.5, xend = x + 0.5,
             y = y - 0.5, yend = y + 0.5))

# Horizontal edges: separate vertically adjacent points (5 x 2 = 10 edges)
h_edges <- with(expand.grid(x = 1:5, y = 1:2),
  data.frame(x = x - 0.5, xend = x + 0.5,
             y = y + 0.5, yend = y + 0.5))

edges <- rbind(v_edges, h_edges)

# Randomly keep ~60% of the interior edges
drop_prob <- 0.4
edges <- edges[runif(nrow(edges)) > drop_prob, ]

# Outer bounding rectangle (always kept)
rect <- data.frame(xmin = 0.5, xmax = 5.5, ymin = 0.5, ymax = 3.5)

ggplot() +
  geom_rect(data = rect,
            aes(xmin = xmin, xmax = xmax, ymin = ymin, ymax = ymax),
            fill = NA, colour = "black", linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_segment(data = edges,
               aes(x = x, y = y, xend = xend, yend = yend),
               colour = "steelblue", linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_point(data = pts, aes(x, y), colour = "firebrick", size = 3) +
  coord_fixed() +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(title = "Grid Voronoi with random boundaries removed",
       x = NULL, y = NULL)

```

#### With p5.js
```{=html}
<div id="p5-step2"></div>
<script>
(function () {
  const HOST = 'p5-step2';
  const SEED = 42, DROP = 0.4;                         // DROP = probability an edge is removed
  const NX = 5, NY = 3, S = 110, M = 40;
  const sx = x => M + (x - 0.5) * S;
  const sy = y => M + (NY + 0.5 - y) * S;

  function rng(a) {                                    // seeded PRNG (mulberry32)
    return function () {
      a |= 0; a = a + 0x6D2B79F5 | 0;
      let t = Math.imul(a ^ a >>> 15, 1 | a);
      t = t + Math.imul(t ^ t >>> 7, 61 | t) ^ t;
      return ((t ^ t >>> 14) >>> 0) / 4294967296;
    };
  }
  function allEdges() {
    const e = [];
    for (let y = 1; y <= 3; y++) for (let x = 1; x <= 4; x++) e.push([x + .5, y - .5, x + .5, y + .5]);
    for (let y = 1; y <= 2; y++) for (let x = 1; x <= 5; x++) e.push([x - .5, y + .5, x + .5, y + .5]);
    return e;
  }
  function makeEdges(seed, drop) {                     // returns kept and removed edges
    const r = rng(seed), kept = [], removed = [];
    allEdges().forEach(e => (r() > drop ? kept : removed).push(e));
    return { kept, removed };
  }

  new p5(function (p) {
    let seed = SEED;
    p.setup = function () {
      p.createCanvas(NX * S + 2 * M, NY * S + 2 * M);
      p.colorMode(p.HSB, 360, 100, 100);
      p.noLoop();
    };
    p.mousePressed = function () {                     // click the canvas for a new layout
      if (p.mouseX >= 0 && p.mouseX < p.width && p.mouseY >= 0 && p.mouseY < p.height) { seed++; p.redraw(); }
    };
    p.draw = function () {
      const { kept, removed } = makeEdges(seed, DROP);
      p.background(0, 0, 100);
      p.strokeCap(p.SQUARE);
      p.stroke(0, 0, 80); p.strokeWeight(1.5);         // removed edges: faint dotted
      p.drawingContext.setLineDash([3, 5]);
      removed.forEach(([x1, y1, x2, y2]) => p.line(sx(x1), sy(y1), sx(x2), sy(y2)));
      p.drawingContext.setLineDash([]);
      p.stroke(0, 0, 0); p.strokeWeight(5);            // surviving mirrors
      kept.forEach(([x1, y1, x2, y2]) => p.line(sx(x1), sy(y1), sx(x2), sy(y2)));
      p.noFill(); p.rect(sx(0.5), sy(3.5), NX * S, NY * S);
      p.noStroke(); p.fill(0, 85, 70);
      for (let j = 1; j <= NY; j++) for (let i = 1; i <= NX; i++) p.circle(sx(i), sy(j), 9);
      p.fill(0, 0, 30); p.textSize(14);
      p.text(`seed ${seed}, drop ${DROP}: ${kept.length} mirrors kept (click for new seed)`, M, 24);
    };
  }, document.getElementById(HOST) || undefined);
})();
</script>
```
:::

### Step 3: Let there be light and mirrors

Now let us pretend that these boundaries are double-sided mirrors. And further that as mathemagicians, we can we insert a ray of light diagonally into any cell and watch it bounce around. 

The resultant *light paths* could look like @fig-mirrors-light-rays:

::: {.panel-tabset .nav-pills style="background: whitesmoke; "}

#### With R
```{r}
#| label: fig-mirrors-light-rays
#| code-fold: true
#| fig-cap: "2-Way Mirrors and Light Rays"
#| 

# ---- 1. Mirror layout (same construction as the previous chunk) ----------
make_edges <- function(seed = 42, drop_prob = 0.4) {
  set.seed(seed)
  v <- with(expand.grid(x = 1:4, y = 1:3),
            data.frame(x = x + 0.5, xend = x + 0.5, y = y - 0.5, yend = y + 0.5))
  h <- with(expand.grid(x = 1:5, y = 1:2),
            data.frame(x = x - 0.5, xend = x + 0.5, y = y + 0.5, yend = y + 0.5))
  e <- rbind(v, h)
  e[runif(nrow(e)) > drop_prob, ]
}

# ---- 2. Ray tracing ------------------------------------------------------
trace_loops <- function(edges, nx = 5, ny = 3) {

  # Keys for the surviving interior mirrors
  vert <- edges$x == edges$xend
  keep <- c(
    sprintf("V%.2f,%.2f", edges$x[vert],  (edges$y[vert]  + edges$yend[vert]) / 2),
    sprintf("H%.2f,%.2f", (edges$x[!vert] + edges$xend[!vert]) / 2, edges$y[!vert])
  )

  is_half <- function(a) abs(a - round(a)) > 0.25

  # Apply the wall at point p to direction d (reflect if mirror, else pass)
  interact <- function(p, d) {
    if (is_half(p[1])) {                       # vertical wall at x = p[1]
      m <- p[1] %in% c(0.5, nx + 0.5) ||
           sprintf("V%.2f,%.2f", p[1], p[2]) %in% keep
      if (m) d[1] <- -d[1]
    } else {                                   # horizontal wall at y = p[2]
      m <- p[2] %in% c(0.5, ny + 0.5) ||
           sprintf("H%.2f,%.2f", p[1], p[2]) %in% keep
      if (m) d[2] <- -d[2]
    }
    d
  }

  chord_id <- function(p, d) sprintf("%.2f,%.2f", p[1] + 0.25 * d[1], p[2] + 0.25 * d[2])

  # Every cell has 4 chords (a diamond); each is a possible starting segment
  starts <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_len(nx * ny), function(k) {
    i <- (k - 1) %% nx + 1; j <- (k - 1) %/% nx + 1
    data.frame(px = c(i - .5, i, i + .5, i), py = c(j, j + .5, j, j - .5),
               dx = c(1, 1, -1, -1),         dy = c(1, -1, -1, 1))
  }))

  used <- character(0)
  loops <- list()

  for (s in seq_len(nrow(starts))) {
    p0 <- c(starts$px[s], starts$py[s]); d0 <- c(starts$dx[s], starts$dy[s])
    if (chord_id(p0, d0) %in% used) next

    p <- p0; d <- d0
    path <- list(p)
    repeat {
      used <- c(used, chord_id(p, d))
      p <- p + 0.5 * d
      d <- interact(p, d)
      path[[length(path) + 1]] <- p
      if (all(p == p0) && all(d == d0)) break
    }
    loops[[length(loops) + 1]] <- data.frame(do.call(rbind, path)) |>
      setNames(c("x", "y")) |>
      transform(loop = length(loops) + 1)
  }
  do.call(rbind, loops)
}

# ---- 3. Run and plot -----------------------------------------------------
edges <- make_edges(seed = 42, drop_prob = 0.4)
paths <- trace_loops(edges)
paths$loop <- factor(paths$loop)

cat("Number of closed light loops:", nlevels(paths$loop), "\n")

pts  <- expand.grid(x = 1:5, y = 1:3)
rect <- data.frame(xmin = 0.5, xmax = 5.5, ymin = 0.5, ymax = 3.5)

ggplot() +
  geom_path(data = paths, aes(x, y, colour = loop, group = loop), linewidth = 2) +
  geom_rect(data = rect, aes(xmin = xmin, xmax = xmax, ymin = ymin, ymax = ymax),
            fill = NA, colour = "black", linewidth = 1.2) +
  geom_segment(data = edges, aes(x = x, y = y, xend = xend, yend = yend),
               colour = "black", linewidth = 1.2) +
  geom_point(data = pts, aes(x, y), colour = "grey40", size = 1.5) +
  coord_fixed() +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position = "none") +
  labs(title = "Closed light paths bouncing between two-sided mirrors",
       x = NULL, y = NULL)

```

#### With p5.js

```{=html}
<div id="p5-step3"></div>
<script>
(function () {
  const HOST = 'p5-step3';
  const SEED = 42, DROP = 0.4;
  const NX = 5, NY = 3, S = 110, M = 40;
  const sx = x => M + (x - 0.5) * S;
  const sy = y => M + (NY + 0.5 - y) * S;

  function rng(a) {
    return function () {
      a |= 0; a = a + 0x6D2B79F5 | 0;
      let t = Math.imul(a ^ a >>> 15, 1 | a);
      t = t + Math.imul(t ^ t >>> 7, 61 | t) ^ t;
      return ((t ^ t >>> 14) >>> 0) / 4294967296;
    };
  }
  function allEdges() {
    const e = [];
    for (let y = 1; y <= 3; y++) for (let x = 1; x <= 4; x++) e.push([x + .5, y - .5, x + .5, y + .5]);
    for (let y = 1; y <= 2; y++) for (let x = 1; x <= 5; x++) e.push([x - .5, y + .5, x + .5, y + .5]);
    return e;
  }
  function makeKept(seed, drop) {
    const r = rng(seed);
    return allEdges().filter(() => r() > drop);
  }

  // Trace every closed light loop. Returns an array of loops, each an array of {x, y}.
  function traceLoops(kept) {
    const mirrors = new Set(kept.map(([x1, y1, x2, y2]) => Math.round(x1 + x2) + ',' + Math.round(y1 + y2)));
    const isMirror = (ux, uy) => mirrors.has(ux + ',' + uy);

    function interact(ux, uy, dx, dy) {                // reflect at mirrors, pass through gaps
      if (ux % 2 !== 0) {                              // vertical wall
        if (ux === 1 || ux === 2 * NX + 1 || isMirror(ux, uy)) dx = -dx;
      } else {                                         // horizontal wall
        if (uy === 1 || uy === 2 * NY + 1 || isMirror(ux, uy)) dy = -dy;
      }
      return [dx, dy];
    }
    const chord = (ux, uy, dx, dy) => (2 * ux + dx) + ',' + (2 * uy + dy);

    const starts = [];                                 // 4 diamond chords per cell
    for (let j = 1; j <= NY; j++) for (let i = 1; i <= NX; i++)
      starts.push([2 * i - 1, 2 * j, 1, 1], [2 * i, 2 * j + 1, 1, -1],
                  [2 * i + 1, 2 * j, -1, -1], [2 * i, 2 * j - 1, -1, 1]);

    const used = new Set(), loops = [];
    for (const [a, b, c, d] of starts) {
      if (used.has(chord(a, b, c, d))) continue;
      let ux = a, uy = b, dx = c, dy = d;
      const pts = [];
      do {
        used.add(chord(ux, uy, dx, dy));
        pts.push({ x: ux / 2, y: uy / 2 });
        ux += dx; uy += dy;
        [dx, dy] = interact(ux, uy, dx, dy);
      } while (!(ux === a && uy === b && dx === c && dy === d));
      loops.push(pts);
    }
    return loops;
  }

  new p5(function (p) {
    let seed = SEED;
    p.setup = function () {
      p.createCanvas(NX * S + 2 * M, NY * S + 2 * M);
      p.colorMode(p.HSB, 360, 100, 100);
      p.noLoop();
    };
    p.mousePressed = function () {
      if (p.mouseX >= 0 && p.mouseX < p.width && p.mouseY >= 0 && p.mouseY < p.height) { seed++; p.redraw(); }
    };
    p.draw = function () {
      const kept = makeKept(seed, DROP);
      const loops = traceLoops(kept);
      p.background(0, 0, 100);
      p.noFill(); p.strokeWeight(2.5); p.strokeJoin(p.ROUND);
      loops.forEach((pts, k) => {
        p.stroke((k * 137.5) % 360, 80, 85);
        p.beginShape();
        pts.forEach(q => p.vertex(sx(q.x), sy(q.y)));
        p.endShape(p.CLOSE);
      });
      p.stroke(0, 0, 0); p.strokeWeight(5); p.strokeCap(p.SQUARE);
      kept.forEach(([x1, y1, x2, y2]) => p.line(sx(x1), sy(y1), sx(x2), sy(y2)));
      p.noFill(); p.rect(sx(0.5), sy(3.5), NX * S, NY * S);
      p.noStroke(); p.fill(0, 0, 50);
      for (let j = 1; j <= NY; j++) for (let i = 1; i <= NX; i++) p.circle(sx(i), sy(j), 5);
      p.fill(0, 0, 30); p.textSize(14);
      p.text(`seed ${seed}: ${loops.length} closed loop(s) (click for new seed)`, M, 24);
    };
  }, document.getElementById(HOST) || undefined);
})();
</script>
```

:::

This is almost a `kolam`! But not `monolinear`! How can we make it more like a `kolam`? 


### Step 4: Bend the Light

Let's bend the laws of physics and bend the light to reflect off the mirrors using `bezier curves`, rather than straight lines! Here is what we might get @fig-curved-reflections:

::: {.panel-tabset .nav-pills style="background: whitesmoke; "}

#### With R
```{r}
#| label: fig-curved-reflections
#| code-fold: true
#| fig-cap: "Curved Reflections"
#| 
# ---- Curved reflections: reuses `paths`, `edges`, `pts`, `rect` ----------
stopifnot(exists("paths"), exists("edges"), exists("pts"), exists("rect"))

# Largest achievable gap for a given curvature (see notes)
max_gap <- function(curvature) 0.25 - 0.1875 * curvature

# Round off one closed loop. v: data frame x, y (last row repeats the first)
curve_loop <- function(v, s, w, n) {
  v   <- as.matrix(v[, c("x", "y")])
  v   <- v[-nrow(v), , drop = FALSE]            # drop duplicated closing point
  N   <- nrow(v)
  prv <- c(N, seq_len(N - 1))
  nxt <- c(2:N, 1)
  d_in  <- (v - v[prv, ]) / 0.5                 # direction of arriving chord
  d_out <- (v[nxt, ] - v) / 0.5                 # direction of leaving chord
  t <- seq(0, 1, length.out = n)

  out <- vector("list", N)
  for (k in seq_len(N)) {
    m <- v[k, ]
    if (all(d_in[k, ] == d_out[k, ])) {         # ray passes through: no bounce
      out[[k]] <- matrix(m, nrow = 1)
      next
    }
    P0 <- m - s * d_in[k, ]                     # curve leaves the incoming ray
    P3 <- m + s * d_out[k, ]                    # curve rejoins the outgoing ray
    P1 <- P0 + w * (m - P0)                     # control points pulled toward
    P2 <- P3 + w * (m - P3)                     # the mirror point by w
    out[[k]] <- outer((1 - t)^3, P0) + outer(3 * (1 - t)^2 * t, P1) +
                outer(3 * (1 - t) * t^2, P2) + outer(t^3, P3)
  }
  res <- do.call(rbind, out)
  res <- rbind(res, res[1, ])                   # close the loop
  setNames(as.data.frame(res), c("x", "y"))
}

# gap       : distance from the mirror to the apex of each curve (grid units)
# curvature : 0 = straight chamfer across the corner, 1 = fully rounded bend
curve_paths <- function(paths, gap = 0.05, curvature = 0.7, n = 25) {
  stopifnot(gap >= 0, curvature >= 0, curvature <= 1)

  s <- 4 * gap / (4 - 3 * curvature)            # setback along the rays
  if (s > 0.25) {                               # neighbouring bounces would collide
    warning(sprintf("gap %.3f too large for curvature %.2f; using max gap %.3f",
                    gap, curvature, max_gap(curvature)))
    s <- 0.25
  }

  pieces <- lapply(split(paths, paths$loop), curve_loop, s = s, w = curvature, n = n)
  out <- do.call(rbind, Map(function(d, id) { d$loop <- id; d },
                            pieces, names(pieces)))
  out$loop <- factor(out$loop, levels = levels(paths$loop))
  out
}

# ---- Run and plot --------------------------------------------------------
curved <- curve_paths(paths, gap = 0.1, curvature = 0.75)

ggplot() +
  geom_path(data = curved, aes(x, y, colour = loop, group = loop), linewidth = 2) +
  geom_rect(data = rect, aes(xmin = xmin, xmax = xmax, ymin = ymin, ymax = ymax),
            fill = NA, colour = "black", linewidth = 1.2) +
  geom_segment(data = edges, aes(x = x, y = y, xend = xend, yend = yend),
               colour = "black", linewidth = 1.2) +
  geom_point(data = pts, aes(x, y), colour = "grey40", size = 1.5) +
  coord_fixed() +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position = "none") +
  labs(title = "Curved reflections off two-sided mirrors", x = NULL, y = NULL)

# Notes:
# Gap: this is the perpendicular distance from the mirror to the apex of the curve, in grid units where neighbouring points are 1 apart. gap = 0 reproduces the sharp geometric bounce.
# Curvature: at 0, the corner is cut by a straight chord with two abrupt kinks. At 1, the bend is spread out into a smooth arc. The curve is tangent to the incoming and outgoing rays for any curvature above 0.
# Limit on the gap: each chord has a bounce at both ends and is 0.5 long, so each curve can start at most 0.25 from its mirror point. That makes the maximum gap 0.25 - 0.1875 * curvature, which is 0.25 at curvature 0 but only about 0.06 at curvature 1. Larger requests are clamped with a warning. If you need bigger gaps with round bends, the bounces would have to be spaced further apart, for example by using a coarser mirror grid.
# Topology: the loops and the cells they fill are unchanged, because the curves replace only the vertex geometry, not the tracing. So all 15 cells are still covered, and the loop count printed earlier still applies.

```

#### With p5.js
```{=html}
<div id="p5-step4"></div>
<script>
(function () {
  const HOST = 'p5-step4';
  const SEED = 42, DROP = 0.4;
  const GAP = 0.05;            // apex distance from mirror, 0 <= GAP <= 0.25 - 0.1875*CURVATURE
  const CURVATURE = 0.8;       // 0 = straight chamfer, 1 = roundest bend
  const NPTS = 25;             // points per curve
  const NX = 5, NY = 3, S = 110, M = 40;
  const sx = x => M + (x - 0.5) * S;
  const sy = y => M + (NY + 0.5 - y) * S;

  function rng(a) {
    return function () {
      a |= 0; a = a + 0x6D2B79F5 | 0;
      let t = Math.imul(a ^ a >>> 15, 1 | a);
      t = t + Math.imul(t ^ t >>> 7, 61 | t) ^ t;
      return ((t ^ t >>> 14) >>> 0) / 4294967296;
    };
  }
  function allEdges() {
    const e = [];
    for (let y = 1; y <= 3; y++) for (let x = 1; x <= 4; x++) e.push([x + .5, y - .5, x + .5, y + .5]);
    for (let y = 1; y <= 2; y++) for (let x = 1; x <= 5; x++) e.push([x - .5, y + .5, x + .5, y + .5]);
    return e;
  }
  function makeKept(seed, drop) {
    const r = rng(seed);
    return allEdges().filter(() => r() > drop);
  }

  function traceLoops(kept) {
    const mirrors = new Set(kept.map(([x1, y1, x2, y2]) => Math.round(x1 + x2) + ',' + Math.round(y1 + y2)));
    const isMirror = (ux, uy) => mirrors.has(ux + ',' + uy);
    function interact(ux, uy, dx, dy) {
      if (ux % 2 !== 0) { if (ux === 1 || ux === 2 * NX + 1 || isMirror(ux, uy)) dx = -dx; }
      else              { if (uy === 1 || uy === 2 * NY + 1 || isMirror(ux, uy)) dy = -dy; }
      return [dx, dy];
    }
    const chord = (ux, uy, dx, dy) => (2 * ux + dx) + ',' + (2 * uy + dy);
    const starts = [];
    for (let j = 1; j <= NY; j++) for (let i = 1; i <= NX; i++)
      starts.push([2 * i - 1, 2 * j, 1, 1], [2 * i, 2 * j + 1, 1, -1],
                  [2 * i + 1, 2 * j, -1, -1], [2 * i, 2 * j - 1, -1, 1]);
    const used = new Set(), loops = [];
    for (const [a, b, c, d] of starts) {
      if (used.has(chord(a, b, c, d))) continue;
      let ux = a, uy = b, dx = c, dy = d;
      const pts = [];
      do {
        used.add(chord(ux, uy, dx, dy));
        pts.push({ x: ux / 2, y: uy / 2 });
        ux += dx; uy += dy;
        [dx, dy] = interact(ux, uy, dx, dy);
      } while (!(ux === a && uy === b && dx === c && dy === d));
      loops.push(pts);
    }
    return loops;
  }

  // Replace each bounce vertex with a cubic Bezier that stops short of the mirror.
  function curveLoop(v, s, w, n) {
    const N = v.length, out = [];
    for (let k = 0; k < N; k++) {
      const a = v[(k + N - 1) % N], m = v[k], b = v[(k + 1) % N];
      const dix = (m.x - a.x) / 0.5, diy = (m.y - a.y) / 0.5;   // incoming direction
      const dox = (b.x - m.x) / 0.5, doy = (b.y - m.y) / 0.5;   // outgoing direction
      if (dix === dox && diy === doy) { out.push({ x: m.x, y: m.y }); continue; }   // no bounce
      const P0 = { x: m.x - s * dix, y: m.y - s * diy };
      const P3 = { x: m.x + s * dox, y: m.y + s * doy };
      const P1 = { x: P0.x + w * (m.x - P0.x), y: P0.y + w * (m.y - P0.y) };
      const P2 = { x: P3.x + w * (m.x - P3.x), y: P3.y + w * (m.y - P3.y) };
      for (let i = 0; i < n; i++) {
        const t = i / (n - 1), u = 1 - t;
        out.push({
          x: u*u*u*P0.x + 3*u*u*t*P1.x + 3*u*t*t*P2.x + t*t*t*P3.x,
          y: u*u*u*P0.y + 3*u*u*t*P1.y + 3*u*t*t*P2.y + t*t*t*P3.y
        });
      }
    }
    return out;
  }

  new p5(function (p) {
    let seed = SEED;
    p.setup = function () {
      p.createCanvas(NX * S + 2 * M, NY * S + 2 * M);
      p.colorMode(p.HSB, 360, 100, 100);
      p.noLoop();
    };
    p.mousePressed = function () {
      if (p.mouseX >= 0 && p.mouseX < p.width && p.mouseY >= 0 && p.mouseY < p.height) { seed++; p.redraw(); }
    };
    p.draw = function () {
      const c = p.constrain(CURVATURE, 0, 1);
      const maxGap = 0.25 - 0.1875 * c;
      const gap = p.constrain(GAP, 0, maxGap);                // clamp to the valid range
      if (gap !== GAP) console.warn(`GAP ${GAP} too large for curvature ${c}; using ${gap.toFixed(3)}`);
      const s = 4 * gap / (4 - 3 * c);                        // setback along each ray

      const kept = makeKept(seed, DROP);
      const loops = traceLoops(kept);
      p.background(0, 0, 100);
      p.noFill(); p.strokeWeight(2.5); p.strokeJoin(p.ROUND);
      loops.forEach((pts, k) => {
        p.stroke((k * 137.5) % 360, 80, 85);
        p.beginShape();
        curveLoop(pts, s, c, NPTS).forEach(q => p.vertex(sx(q.x), sy(q.y)));
        p.endShape(p.CLOSE);
      });
      p.stroke(0, 0, 0); p.strokeWeight(5); p.strokeCap(p.SQUARE);
      kept.forEach(([x1, y1, x2, y2]) => p.line(sx(x1), sy(y1), sx(x2), sy(y2)));
      p.noFill(); p.rect(sx(0.5), sy(3.5), NX * S, NY * S);
      p.noStroke(); p.fill(0, 0, 50);
      for (let j = 1; j <= NY; j++) for (let i = 1; i <= NX; i++) p.circle(sx(i), sy(j), 5);
      p.fill(0, 0, 30); p.textSize(14);
      p.text(`seed ${seed}: ${loops.length} loop(s), gap ${gap.toFixed(3)} (max ${maxGap.toFixed(3)}), curvature ${c}`, M, 24);
    };
  }, document.getElementById(HOST) || undefined);
})();
</script>
```
:::




::: {.content-hidden}
Hard limits (enforced by stopifnot in curve_paths()):

Curvature: 0 ≤ curvature ≤ 1. At 0 the corner is a straight chamfer, and at 1 it is the roundest bend. Above 1 the Bézier control points overshoot the mirror point and the curve develops loops, so it is rejected.
Gap: 0 ≤ gap ≤ 0.25 - 0.1875 * curvature. At 0 you get the sharp geometric bounce. The upper bound depends on curvature, so the two parameters are not independent. If you exceed it, the code clamps the gap to the maximum and warns.

Maximum gap by curvature (grid units, neighbouring points 1 apart):

|curvature|	max gap|
0.00 |	0.250 |
0.25 |	0.203 |
0.50 |	0.156 |
0.75 |	0.109 |
1.00 |	0.063 |

Why the limit has this shape: the curve starts a setback s back along the incoming ray and rejoins the outgoing ray s after the mirror. The apex gap works out to gap = s(4 - 3·curvature)/4. Each chord is 0.5 long in the code's direction units and may have a bounce at both ends, so s can be at most 0.25 before the two curves meet at the chord's midpoint. Setting s = 0.25 gives the maximum gap above.

Practical guidance:

Stay at roughly 90% of the maximum or less. At the exact limit, neighbouring curves touch at chord midpoints and the path no longer has a straight segment between bounces.
Good starting values are curvature = 0.5–0.8 with gap = 0.03–0.08.
For a large gap with a round bend, the bounces would need to be spaced further apart, which means a coarser mirror grid.

If you want the limit checked in code, this helper keeps requests valid:

r
gap_limits <- function(curvature) {
  stopifnot(curvature >= 0, curvature <= 1)
  c(min = 0, max = 0.25 - 0.1875 * curvature)
}

gap_limits(0.8)   # min 0.00, max 0.10
:::

## Discussion

- A `kolam` is a curved rendering of a `Voronoi Diagram` of a set of points
- By modelling the Voronoi itself as a set of doubles-sided mirrors, we get the starting point to generate a `kolam` for a set of points
- We can then *insert light* into the grid, and watch it reflect off the mirror-walls of the Voronoi. 
- If we retain the **full Voronoi**, we will get diamonds of light around each point
- If we ***remove parts of the Voronoi** , then the light rays can travel over longer paths, before returning to form some sort of closed path
- And if we make the reflections curvy using `bezier curves`, that is the `kolam`, albeit *not necessarily `monolinear`*

## Design Process

- Generate a set of points on a square grid;
- Enclose these in a logical boundary shape ( rectangle in the above diagrams );
- Generate the Voronoi diagram for the points, and bound the Voronoi with the enclosing shape;
- Remove parts of the Voronoi, where you want the kolam-light-path to continue. Here lies the artistry! Try to remove these in a *symmetric* fashion
- Re-run your code to let the light travel over the new set of paths
- There!!

### Doing this "by hand"

Suppose we hand-draw a grid, and place mirrors wherever we need, and remove them where we don't need them. ( We focus on rectangular outlines for now.). 
We might take a leaf out of R's `{ggplot}` book, and encode the *presence* of a mirror on each edge of a **cell** enclosing a point. We use the letters `t,r,b,l` ( Mnemonic: "trouble") to encode whether a cell has a mirror on `top`, `right`, `bottom`, and `left`. If a mirror exists at `top`, we encode $t=1$ and so on. So each cell then has a `4-bit` 1/0 pattern to encode the presence of mirrors. 

::: {.panel-tabset .nav-pills style="background: whitesmoke; "}

#### With R

```{r}
#| code-fold: true
#| 
# =====================================================================
# Self-contained: mirror layout -> "trbl" matrix (ny x nx, row 1 = top)
# Each interior mirror appears in both neighbouring cells.
# =====================================================================
nx <- 5; ny <- 3

# ---- 1. Random mirror layout (data frame: x, y, xend, yend) ----------
make_edges <- function(seed = 42, drop_prob = 0.4) {
  set.seed(seed)
  v <- with(expand.grid(x = 1:4, y = 1:3),
            data.frame(x = x + .5, xend = x + .5, y = y - .5, yend = y + .5))
  h <- with(expand.grid(x = 1:5, y = 1:2),
            data.frame(x = x - .5, xend = x + .5, y = y + .5, yend = y + .5))
  e <- rbind(v, h)
  e[runif(nrow(e)) > drop_prob, ]
}

# ---- 2. edges -> trbl matrix ------------------------------------------
edges_to_trbl <- function(edges, nx = 5, ny = 3) {
  top <- right <- bottom <- left <- matrix(FALSE, ny, nx)
  top[1, ] <- bottom[ny, ] <- left[, 1] <- right[, nx] <- TRUE   # outer rectangle
  for (k in seq_len(nrow(edges))) {
    e <- edges[k, ]
    if (e$x == e$xend) {                          # vertical mirror
      r  <- ny - round((e$y + e$yend) / 2) + 1
      cc <- round(e$x - .5)
      right[r, cc] <- left[r, cc + 1] <- TRUE
    } else {                                      # horizontal mirror
      r  <- round(ny - e$y + .5)
      cc <- round((e$x + e$xend) / 2)
      bottom[r, cc] <- top[r + 1, cc] <- TRUE
    }
  }
  matrix(paste0(+top, +right, +bottom, +left), ny, nx)
}

# ---- 3. trbl matrix -> edges (with validation) ------------------------
code_to_edges <- function(M, nx = 5, ny = 3) {
  stopifnot("M must be ny x nx" = is.matrix(M) && nrow(M) == ny && ncol(M) == nx,
            "entries must be 4 characters of 0/1 (t,r,b,l)" = all(grepl("^[01]{4}$", M)))
  bit <- function(k) matrix(substr(M, k, k) == "1", nrow = ny)
  top <- bit(1); right <- bit(2); bottom <- bit(3); left <- bit(4)

  if (!all(top[1, ]) || !all(bottom[ny, ]) || !all(left[, 1]) || !all(right[, nx]))
    stop("Outer sides must be 1 (the bounding rectangle is always a mirror)")

  h <- which(right[, -nx, drop = FALSE] != left[, -1, drop = FALSE], arr.ind = TRUE)
  if (nrow(h))
    stop("Right side of [", h[1, 1], ",", h[1, 2], "] disagrees with left side of [",
         h[1, 1], ",", h[1, 2] + 1, "]")
  v <- which(bottom[-ny, , drop = FALSE] != top[-1, , drop = FALSE], arr.ind = TRUE)
  if (nrow(v))
    stop("Bottom side of [", v[1, 1], ",", v[1, 2], "] disagrees with top side of [",
         v[1, 1] + 1, ",", v[1, 2], "]")

  e <- which(right[, -nx, drop = FALSE], arr.ind = TRUE)
  s <- which(bottom[-ny, , drop = FALSE], arr.ind = TRUE)
  rbind(
    data.frame(x = e[, 2] + .5, xend = e[, 2] + .5,
               y = ny - e[, 1] + .5, yend = ny - e[, 1] + 1.5),
    data.frame(x = s[, 2] - .5, xend = s[, 2] + .5,
               y = ny - s[, 1] + .5, yend = ny - s[, 1] + .5)
  )
}

# ---- 4. Edit one mirror, keeping both copies in sync -------------------
set_mirror <- function(M, row, col, side, value = 0) {
  put <- function(M, r, c, k) {
    s <- strsplit(M[r, c], "")[[1]]; s[k] <- as.character(value)
    M[r, c] <- paste(s, collapse = ""); M
  }
  M <- put(M, row, col, match(side, c("t", "r", "b", "l")))
  if (side == "t" && row > 1)        M <- put(M, row - 1, col, 3)
  if (side == "r" && col < ncol(M))  M <- put(M, row, col + 1, 4)
  if (side == "b" && row < nrow(M))  M <- put(M, row + 1, col, 1)
  if (side == "l" && col > 1)        M <- put(M, row, col - 1, 2)
  M
}

# ---- 5. Print as a grid, optionally CSV and a paste-ready JS literal ---
print_trbl <- function(M, file = NULL, js = FALSE) {
  cat(apply(M, 1, paste, collapse = " "), sep = "\n")
  if (!is.null(file))
    write.table(M, file, sep = ",", quote = FALSE, row.names = FALSE, col.names = FALSE)
  if (js) {
    rows <- apply(M, 1, function(r) paste0('["', paste(r, collapse = '","'), '"]'))
    cat("\nlet ADJ = [", paste(rows, collapse = ",\n           "), "];\n", sep = "")
  }
  invisible(M)
}

# =========================== RUN =====================================
edges <- make_edges(42, 0.4)
M <- edges_to_trbl(edges)
print_trbl(M, js = TRUE)                      # add file = "mirrors.csv" to save

# Hand edit: remove the mirror between row 2/col 3 and row 2/col 4
M2 <- set_mirror(M, 2, 3, "r", 0)
print_trbl(M2)

# Round-trip check (should print TRUE)
identical(edges_to_trbl(code_to_edges(M2)), M2)

# Full Voronoi, for comparison: every cell is "1111"
print_trbl(matrix("1111", ny, nx))

```

#### With p5.js

```{=html}
<div id="p5-trbl"></div>
<script>
(function () {
  const HOST = 'p5-trbl';
  const NX = 5, NY = 3, S = 110, MARGIN = 40, TEXT_H = 90;
  const SEED = 42, DROP = 0.4;

  // Paste a matrix from R here (3 rows x 5 columns, "trbl", row 1 = top), or leave null.
  const INPUT = null;
  // const INPUT = [["1111","1111","1111","1111","1111"],
  //                ["1111","1111","1011","1110","1111"],
  //                ["1111","1111","1111","1111","1111"]];

  const sx = x => MARGIN + (x - 0.5) * S;
  const sy = y => MARGIN + (NY + 0.5 - y) * S;

  // ---- seeded PRNG (mulberry32) ----
  function rng(a) {
    return function () {
      a |= 0; a = a + 0x6D2B79F5 | 0;
      let t = Math.imul(a ^ a >>> 15, 1 | a);
      t = t + Math.imul(t ^ t >>> 7, 61 | t) ^ t;
      return ((t ^ t >>> 14) >>> 0) / 4294967296;
    };
  }

  // ---- all 22 interior edges as [x1, y1, x2, y2] ----
  function allEdges() {
    const e = [];
    for (let y = 1; y <= 3; y++) for (let x = 1; x <= 4; x++) e.push([x + .5, y - .5, x + .5, y + .5]);
    for (let y = 1; y <= 2; y++) for (let x = 1; x <= 5; x++) e.push([x - .5, y + .5, x + .5, y + .5]);
    return e;
  }
  function makeKept(seed, drop) {
    const r = rng(seed);
    return allEdges().filter(() => r() > drop);
  }

  // ---- edges -> NY x NX array of "trbl" strings (row 0 = top) ----
  function edgesToTrbl(kept) {
    const mk = () => Array.from({ length: NY }, () => Array(NX).fill(false));
    const t = mk(), r = mk(), b = mk(), l = mk();
    for (let c = 0; c < NX; c++) { t[0][c] = true; b[NY - 1][c] = true; }
    for (let i = 0; i < NY; i++) { l[i][0] = true; r[i][NX - 1] = true; }
    kept.forEach(([x1, y1, x2, y2]) => {
      if (x1 === x2) {                                   // vertical mirror
        const row = NY - Math.round((y1 + y2) / 2), col = Math.round(x1 - 0.5) - 1;
        r[row][col] = true; l[row][col + 1] = true;
      } else {                                           // horizontal mirror
        const row = NY - Math.round(y1 + 0.5), col = Math.round((x1 + x2) / 2) - 1;
        b[row][col] = true; t[row + 1][col] = true;
      }
    });
    return t.map((rowT, i) => rowT.map((_, j) =>
      `${+t[i][j]}${+r[i][j]}${+b[i][j]}${+l[i][j]}`));
  }

  // ---- "trbl" matrix -> edges, with validation ----
  function trblToEdges(M) {
    if (M.length !== NY || M.some(r => r.length !== NX))
      throw new Error(`matrix must be ${NY} x ${NX}`);
    for (let r = 0; r < NY; r++) for (let c = 0; c < NX; c++)
      if (!/^[01]{4}$/.test(M[r][c])) throw new Error(`[${r+1},${c+1}] must be 4 chars of 0/1 (t,r,b,l)`);
    const b = (r, c, k) => M[r][c][k] === '1';           // k: 0=t 1=r 2=b 3=l
    const edges = [];
    for (let r = 0; r < NY; r++) for (let c = 0; c < NX; c++) {
      if (r === 0      && !b(r, c, 0)) throw new Error(`[${r+1},${c+1}]: top side must be 1`);
      if (r === NY - 1 && !b(r, c, 2)) throw new Error(`[${r+1},${c+1}]: bottom side must be 1`);
      if (c === 0      && !b(r, c, 3)) throw new Error(`[${r+1},${c+1}]: left side must be 1`);
      if (c === NX - 1 && !b(r, c, 1)) throw new Error(`[${r+1},${c+1}]: right side must be 1`);
      const xn = c + 1, yn = NY - r;
      if (c < NX - 1) {
        if (b(r, c, 1) !== b(r, c + 1, 3))
          throw new Error(`[${r+1},${c+1}] right side disagrees with [${r+1},${c+2}] left side`);
        if (b(r, c, 1)) edges.push([xn + .5, yn - .5, xn + .5, yn + .5]);
      }
      if (r < NY - 1) {
        if (b(r, c, 2) !== b(r + 1, c, 0))
          throw new Error(`[${r+1},${c+1}] bottom side disagrees with [${r+2},${c+1}] top side`);
        if (b(r, c, 2)) edges.push([xn - .5, yn - .5, xn + .5, yn - .5]);
      }
    }
    return edges;
  }

  // ---- print: console (grid + paste-ready literal) and return the text ----
  function printTrbl(M) {
    const text = M.map(row => row.join(' ')).join('\n');
    console.log(text);
    console.log('let INPUT = ' + JSON.stringify(M) + ';');
    return text;
  }

  new p5(function (p) {
    p.setup = function () {
      p.createCanvas(NX * S + 2 * MARGIN, NY * S + 2 * MARGIN + TEXT_H);
      p.noLoop();
    };
    p.draw = function () {
      p.background(255);
      let kept, msg = '';
      try {
        kept = INPUT ? trblToEdges(INPUT) : makeKept(SEED, DROP);
      } catch (e) {
        kept = []; msg = 'Error: ' + e.message;
      }
      const trbl = msg ? null : edgesToTrbl(kept);
      const text = trbl ? printTrbl(trbl) : msg;

      p.stroke(0); p.strokeWeight(5); p.strokeCap(p.SQUARE);
      kept.forEach(([x1, y1, x2, y2]) => p.line(sx(x1), sy(y1), sx(x2), sy(y2)));
      p.noFill(); p.rect(sx(0.5), sy(3.5), NX * S, NY * S);
      p.noStroke(); p.fill(170, 40, 40);
      for (let j = 1; j <= NY; j++) for (let i = 1; i <= NX; i++) p.circle(sx(i), sy(j), 9);

      p.fill(40); p.textFont('monospace'); p.textSize(13);
      text.split('\n').forEach((line, i) =>
        p.text(line, MARGIN, NY * S + 2 * MARGIN + 6 + i * 18));
    };
  }, document.getElementById(HOST) || undefined);
})();
</script>
```

The `p5.js` code for generating / inputting your matrix is here <https://editor.p5js.org/arvindv/full/Gx1UD74Fh>

:::


## Wait, But Why?

- There are many ways to creating symmetry and shapes
- For Kolam and Lusona, we have seen matrices, mirrors, knots, and voronoi diagrams as vehicles to visualize and create them
- Which method do you like the most? 
- What is unique about each method?
- How are they related? ( of course!!)
